st.headline: Haze-linked First Resources, Bumitama post higher profits for Q3
st.teaser: Both First Resources and Bumitama reiterated their commitment to upholding a zero-burning policy
fullText: SINGAPORE – Two palm oil companies linked to the transboundary haze in October reported higher profits for the third quarter ended Sept 30, in separate business updates published on the morning of Nov 13.
Palm oil producer First Resources posted a 40.1% rise in its underlying net profit to US$122.7 million (S$158 million) for the third quarter of 2026, from US$87.5 million in the year-ago period.
The increase was boosted by higher sales of palm oil products and fruit bunches harvested from oil palms, it said.
Sales were up 24.9% at US$578.6 million for the quarter, compared with US$463.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation rose 26.6% to US$207.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from US$163.8 million a year ago.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, sales grew 36.5% year on year to US$1.6 billion, driven by higher sales volumes.
A net inventory drawdown of 28,000 tonnes over the nine-month period, compared with a build-up of 80,000 tonnes in the corresponding period in 2025, also supported higher sales volumes.

The group’s stronger production output in the first nine months of 2026 was also attributable in part to the full nine-month contribution from Austindo Nusantara Jaya, an Indonesian agribusiness company acquired in May 2025.
However, profits were partially offset by foreign currency translation losses resulting from the depreciation of the Indonesian rupiah against the US dollar.
The group said it expects demand for palm oil to remain supported by Indonesia’s biodiesel programme.
In addition, elevated crude oil prices arising from geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are expected to support biodiesel economics and crude palm oil demand.

Meanwhile, Bumitama reported a 1.9% increase in its net profit to 614.1 billion rupiah (S$43 million) for the quarter ended Sept 30, compared with 602.9 billion rupiah in the previous corresponding period.
For the nine-month period, net profit rose 30.6% to 2.4 trillion rupiah, up from 1.9 trillion rupiah in the year-ago period.
Revenue increased 9.7% to 4.2 trillion rupiah in the third quarter, up from 3.9 trillion rupiah a year ago. For the nine-month period, revenue was up 20% at 16.3 trillion rupiah.
Bumitama said its performance was supported by productivity improvements in its plantations and mills, particularly during the earlier part of the quarter.
In July, internal production of fresh fruit bunches reached 383,203 tonnes, accounting for almost 40% of the quarter’s production.
Quarterly production of crude palm oil increased 14% year on year to 368,323 tonnes.
However, exceptionally dry weather conditions in its Kalimantan estates during the third quarter put additional pressure on logistics infrastructure and disrupted shipments, said Bumitama.
Consequently, third-quarter revenue declined compared with the second quarter.
The prolonged dry season also heightened the risk of land and forest fires across parts of Kalimantan.
Fires affected certain areas within or adjoining the group’s concessions, including community-managed, conservation and unplanted land, the group noted.

Bumitama said that elevated energy prices and Indonesia’s biodiesel programme coupled with a relatively constrained palm oil supply growth could provide a “supportive backdrop” for palm oil fundamentals heading into 2027.

However, market conditions remain subject to uncertainty. These include changes in global energy prices, supply-and-demand dynamics, and the potential effects of prolonged dry weather on future production, it added.
Both First Resources and Bumitama reiterated their commitment to upholding a zero-burning policy, and cooperating with the Indonesian and Singapore authorities in relation to the haze.
Shares of First Resources closed flat at $2.79 and those of Bumitama closed flat at $1.39 on Nov 12, before the updates. THE BUSINESS TIMES

cna.headline: Burberry defies luxury downturn as trench coats and scarves power revival
cna.teaser: Fashion group’s sales continue to rise in China and US as strategy of refocusing on core products pays off.
fullText: Buoyant demand for Burberry’s scarves and trench coats helped the UK’s leading luxury brand sustain its rebound in sales, bucking a trend of worsening performance across the industry.

The FTSE 100 company’s comparable sales rose 4 per cent in the three months to September 26, ahead of analysts’ expectations, outperforming larger rivals such as LVMH and Gucci owner Kering. Burberry’s adjusted operating profit rose to £62 million (US$82.01 million; S$105.53 million) in the first half of the year, above forecasts of £44 million.

The luxury industry’s downturn has been driven primarily by weaker sales in China, an engine of growth for decades. Burberry, however, reported a 5 per cent rise in comparable sales in the country during the second quarter after delivering 9 per cent growth in the previous quarter.

Chief executive Joshua Schulman said: “Luxury customers around the world, but particularly in China, are experiencing some fatigue with exorbitant pricing, and in this context our strategy of having enduring value and providing great value for money is resonating strongly with the Chinese customers.”
Bernstein analyst Luca Solca noted that Burberry’s overall growth was “almost as good as Hermes and 9 percentage points better than LVMH’s fashion and leather goods division in the same quarter”.
The company’s strongest region was the Americas, predominantly the US, where sales rose 11 per cent in the second quarter. Burberry’s shares rose 7 per cent in morning trading on Thursday.

The results are a boost to Schulman, who was appointed in 2024 to lead a turnaround of the UK’s pre-eminent luxury brand after it made an ill-timed push upmarket just as demand for luxury goods began to wilt.
Schulman said on Thursday that Burberry’s ability to outperform the luxury market gave him “increasing confidence” that his revival plan was “the right path”.

Burberry has enlisted British celebrities such as actors Pierce Brosnan and Fiona Shaw for campaigns promoting the brand’s renewed focus on its signature products such as trench coats and scarves. The brand has also focused on providing more affordable products at a time when “aspirational” luxury consumers are less willing to spend.
Last year, it announced a major restructuring plan to cut almost a fifth of its workforce to help save £100 million in annual costs by early next year.

The company counts Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group as an investor. The high street tycoon told the FT this summer that he was driven to invest in Burberry — which is stocked in Frasers’ Flannels chain — because of a belief in Schulman’s turnaround.

Burberry investor Kernow Asset Management said its turnaround was “progressing well, outperforming its peers this year and delivering a fifth consecutive quarter of growth”. They added that the next phase of its revival was “taking shape” as the fashion brand prepares to update investors on its strategy in March.
